sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 12.8% a year from $4,860.4m in FY2016 to $14,342.9m in FY2025 [F1][F10][F198], but the path was a step change, not a smooth climb.
FY2021 revenue jumped 89.1% to $16,071.7m [F6][D241], driven by REGEN-COV US sales of $5,828.0m that contributed 66.4pp of growth [S48][D582].

FY2022 revenue fell 24.3% to $12,172.9m [F7][D292] as REGEN-COV dropped to zero [S49][D585], and growth since has been single-digit: 7.8% in FY2023, 8.3% in FY2024 and 1.0% in FY2025 [D342][D391][D440].
Operating margin peaked at 55.7% in FY2021 [F26][D750] and has fallen for four straight years to 24.9% in FY2025 [F30][D749], a 30.7pp decline [R1].
The mix has inverted: net product sales fell 17.3% in FY2025 and contributed -9.3pp to growth [D506][D507], while collaboration revenue rose 21.0% and contributed +9.0pp [D522][D523].
Regeneron's share of Sanofi antibody profits reached $5,241.6m, 36.5% of revenue, and added 9.3pp of growth in FY2025 [S52][D590][D592].
That share rose on higher Dupixent sales [P9], while the Bayer EYLEA profit share fell 8.6% to $1,282.7m on lower ex-US EYLEA sales [S118][D731][P8].

US EYLEA sales fell 42.4% to $2,747.8m, a -14.2pp drag, on competitive pressure, compounded bevacizumab and the EYLEA HD transition [S43][D577][D578][P10]; EYLEA HD rose 36.3% to $1,636.9m [S64][D613][P11].
Operating income fell 10.3% in FY2025 against 1.0% revenue growth [D441][D440], and operating expenses grew 5.4% [D457], so there was no operating leverage.
The FY2025 operating margin of 24.9% sits 9.7pp below the window median of 34.6% and at the window low [F30][D751][D749].
The FY2025 bridge is R&D -4.7pp, other lines -0.5pp, partly offset by SG&A +2.0pp [D465][D467][D466].
R&D rose 14.0% to $5,850.2m, or 40.8% of revenue [D455][X34][D420], the highest share in the window [D759]; the filing describes program spending but gives no single cause for the increase [P6].
SG&A fell 8.6% to $2,700.0m [D456][X47], primarily on lower charitable contributions to Good Days [P5].
Net margin held at 31.4% [F50] because other income reached $1,652.8m [X117], and the 13.9% effective tax rate was helped by the IRS audit settlement [D427][P2].
Operating cash flow was $4,978.9m and free cash flow $4,080.5m in FY2025 [F80][F100], a 28.4% free-cash-flow margin [D425].
Free cash flow covered net income 0.91x [D429], below the window median of 0.88x only marginally but below the peer median of 1.11x [D763][D783].
Capex rose 18.9% to $898.4m, 6.3% of revenue and 1.65x D&A [D447][F90][D424][D430], part of a multi-year build-out [P19].
Stock-based compensation was $993.7m, 20.0% of operating cash flow [X77][D431], a persistent non-cash add-back.
Cash and investments reached $18,865.8m against $1,985.9m of debt [D432][D433], for net cash of $16,879.9m, 117.7% of revenue [D434][D435].
That net-cash ratio ranks at the 100th percentile of eight biopharma peers, whose median is -50.7% [D780][D781].
Buybacks plus dividends were $3,808.9m, 93.3% of free cash flow [D436][D437], and the diluted share count fell 5.6% [D459].
A dividend began in FY2025 at $370.3m [X140], while acquisitions were negligible at $3.3m [X145].
Operating margin has fallen four consecutive years, from 55.7% to 24.9%, a 30.7pp decline [F26][F30][R1], with R&D intensity at a window high [D759].
US EYLEA, once 63.0% of revenue [D554], fell to 19.2% [D576] and is still shrinking at 42.4% [D577], so the erosion is structural, not one-off.

Revenue for FY2018 and FY2019 in the table is a later recast, $5,145.6m and $6,557.6m against $6,710.8m and $7,863.4m first reported [F3][X3][F4][X4][R2], so growth spanning those years mixes presentations.
Free-cash-flow conversion of 0.91x trails the peer median of 1.11x [D429][D783], a mild earnings-quality gap.

If the FY2026 operating margin falls below the FY2025 level of 24.9% [F30], the four-year decline continues; a recovery above the 34.6% window median [D751] would reverse it, reported in the FY2026 10-K.
Watch US EYLEA sales against the FY2025 level of $2,747.8m [S43]: further decline confirms the franchise erosion, while stabilization would mark a turn.
Watch R&D as a share of revenue against the FY2025 40.8% [D420]; a move back toward the 34.6% median [D760] would restore operating leverage.
